title: Are US Long Bonds A Buy? (Part I)

Are US Long Bonds A Buy? (Part I)

Will Denyer

Gavekal Research | 26 Aug 2026

The US Treasury is buying back more of its own long-term debt. Perhaps private investors should take note. The question is whether US long bonds now belong in portfolios, either as outright long positions or as hedges for equities, especially long-duration growth stocks.To answer this question, the first report in this series focuses on the significance of recent policy changes—namely, the US’s unusual foreign exchange intervention, which was really a bond market intervention in disguise, the Treasury’s increased buyback program and the role of the Federal Reserve. Forthcoming installments will then look at increased demand for capital from both the public and private sectors, bond valuations and the usefulness of bonds as a portfolio hedge.
